clue.text: Protection for individual from short wave alarms

indicators.note: short means the word for a wave is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: a billow is a large wave
frights are alarms or scares

explanation.surface: A guarantee of personal safety from the alarms set off by a brief radio wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from the word for a wave. The definition is the constitutional sense: a charter protecting each citizen's liberties.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a charter lists the liberties that guard each citizen against the state.

clue.text: Broadcast from West Berlin half scrambled

indicators.note: scrambled tells us the gathered letters are mixed up
half takes the first three of Berlin's six letters

explanation.surface: Transmissions from West Berlin are partly jammed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is the verb to scatter. 'half' gives BER from Berlin; 'scrambled' rearranges WEST + BER.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew things about is to scatter them widely, as seed is cast.

clue.text: Student with driving ambition

parts.note: read literally, someone whose aim is to drive a car, as a novice with L-plates

explanation.surface: A highly motivated pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving ambition' means intense drive, but read literally it is an ambition to drive: a novice motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice motorist with L-plates is a student whose aim is to drive.

clue.text: Clear command for military formation

parts.note: clear means open, as a clear road
an order is a command

explanation.surface: An unambiguous order given to troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops spaced widely apart in loose ranks make a recognised drill arrangement.

clue.text: Examined carefully, showing stern inclination

definitions.meaning: to have searched through thoroughly, as one goes over evidence
a ship's stern sloping backwards is said to have a rake

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinised closely and looked severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like severe but is the back of a ship; a mast or stern that slopes is said to have a rake.
explanation.definitionFit: Combing through means scrutinising; and nautically a backward slope of mast or stern is a rake.

clue.text: Less discriminating sort of tradesman, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the shopkeeper is spoken out

parts.note: a grocer is a kind of shopkeeper

explanation.surface: A tradesman of some kind with less refined judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: GROCER, a food shopkeeper, is pronounced like the comparative of gross.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarser, cruder taste shows poorer judgment and refinement.

clue.text: Somehow earn, the capital for some Asians

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: Someone manages to earn capital money for a group of Asians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a capital city, here spelt the older way, of Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran's chief city is the seat of government for Iranians.

clue.text: Like the Pentagon's sort of disarmament policy?

definitions.meaning: a pentagon has five sides, so it is many-sided
arms reduction agreed among many nations at once

explanation.surface: A question about the American defence headquarters' approach to arms reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Pentagon' looks like the US defence department, but it is the five-sided shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Having many sides fits a five-sided figure; and arms cuts agreed by several countries form a many-party policy.

clue.text: Get a positional advantage over other player

definitions.text: Get a positional advantage over other player

parts.words: Get a positional advantage over other player
parts.note: read in theatre terms: an actor moving to the back of the stage makes a colleague face away from the audience

explanation.surface: A sportsman jockeys for position over an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'player' is an actor, not a sportsman: standing further from the audience forces the other actor to turn their back on it.
explanation.definitionFit: In stagecraft, drawing focus by standing deeper on stage literally gains a positional edge over a fellow actor.

clue.text: In work? No — who wants this skill?

indicators.note: In tells us the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question asking who would turn down practical expertise that brings work.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical expertise or technical knowledge is a skill.

clue.text: American film is on the French 'part of Scotland

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film from America
taken as written
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: An American cowboy picture is showing on a French screen in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Outer Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast, form this island area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Outer Hebrides form a council area off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Nothing in rent given to North American city

indicators.note: in places the letter for nothing within the word for torn

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, meaning torn
O, the figure zero, means nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nothing in the way of rent is paid to a North American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for housing but is the past participle of rend: torn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian city on Lake Ontario is a major North American conurbation.

clue.text: Wastes what is earned

explanation.surface: Squandering what one has earned.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the phrase 'just deserts', what someone has earned, pronounced like puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren wastelands are arid regions; one's due reward is what one merits.

clue.text: Inferior cow, from what we hear.

definitions.meaning: inferior means of lesser rank or quality
a cow is heard to low, so it is something that lows

explanation.surface: A remark about a poor-quality cow based on rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful noun: a cow moos, or lows, so by its sound it is one that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means beneath in rank; and a bovine mooing makes it, whimsically, a 'low-er'.

clue.text: Backs around monarch in submissive attitude

indicators.note: around shows the word for backs sits on either side of the monarch

parts.note: in football the backs are the defence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Defenders encircle the king, bowing in humility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' are the defensive players in football, the DEFENCE; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a standard crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectful yielding to another's wishes is a humble, submissive stance.

clue.text: Not flaming well fair, initially, getting one rebuke

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of fair

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is one
a reproof is a rebuke

explanation.surface: A mild reprimand for being bloody fair at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaming' looks like a mild British swear word with 'well', but the definition means resistant to burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that resists catching alight will not burn properly.

clue.text: Leader of the engineers, a more positive officer

indicators.note: leader of picks out the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
surer means more certain or positive

explanation.surface: The head of the engineering corps is a more confident officer.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers. The officer is the one who keeps a society's funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A society's money-keeper is one of its elected office-holders.

clue.text: Find fee misused to get foreign title

indicators.note: misused hints the letters are put to a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a fee wrongly charged to obtain an overseas honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an old Turkish honorific for a man of learning or rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Turkish honorific for men of education or standing.

clue.text: Filling glasses — that is kind

indicators.note: filling shows the abbreviation sits inside the word for glasses

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Topping up drinks is a generous act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like generous but is the noun: a sort. 'glasses' are spectacles, not drinking glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological category or sort is a kind.

clue.text: Before fall, spot black bear

indicators.note: Before puts the small piece ahead of the word for fall
a spot of something is a small amount, here the opening letter of black

parts.note: ruin is a downfall or fall

explanation.surface: Before autumn, someone catches sight of a black bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a verb, to see, but means just a dab of 'black': its first letter B. 'Before' puts that B in front of RUIN, a downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A folksy name for a bear, as in old fables.

clue.text: Top gear, look, in some vehicles

indicators.note: in puts the short word for look inside the vehicles

parts.note: buses are vehicles
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Upper gears in some vehicles get a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' suggests a car's highest gear, but it means clothing worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirts for women are upper-body clothing.

clue.text: Inconsistent, more or less

definitions.meaning: either greater or smaller, so not the same amount

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely variable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more or less' usually means approximately, but here means either more or less: not the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven performance is variable; and being bigger or smaller means different in size.

clue.text: Turn back express

explanation.surface: A fast train turning round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a train but is the verb: to show or reveal, as a face shows feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror throws light back; and a choice can show or convey someone's views.

clue.text: Formidable opponent a scratch performer?

definitions.meaning: a big cat uses its claws to scratch

explanation.surface: A fearsome rival who plays off scratch at golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratch' suggests a golfer with no handicap, but the big striped cat claws.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce competitor is likened to the big cat; and the cat uses claws to scratch.

clue.text: One certainly capable of adopting new posture

definitions.text: One certainly capable of adopting new posture

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of posture are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who can strike a fresh pose at will.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the Greek sea god changed his shape at will, and a new form of POSTURE spells his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape-shifting old man of the sea in Greek myth could take on any form.

clue.text: It comes between flights, in more ways than one

definitions.text: It comes between flights, in more ways than one

parts.words: It comes between flights, in more ways than one
parts.note: a level platform separates two runs of stairs, and an aircraft touching down ends one journey before the next

explanation.surface: Something that happens between plane journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are 'between flights': the floor between staircases, and an aircraft's touchdown between trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Stair platforms and aircraft touchdowns both separate one flight from another.

clue.text: Cryptic ending of the book of Jude

definitions.text: ending of the book of Jude
definitions.meaning: Hardy's novel is titled 'Jude the ...', and this word ends that title

explanation.surface: A puzzling conclusion to a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book of Jude' suggests the New Testament epistle, but the book is Thomas Hardy's novel, whose title ends with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means unclear or little known; Hardy's 1895 novel ends its title with that adjective.

clue.text: Initially, no option to buy.

parts.note: initially means at first
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: From the start, there is no chance to purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the right to be offered something before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The right to be offered a purchase before anyone else is a buying option.
